ambiguities: Who should be able to open this page? (a) Anyone who already has the key used for the lab's other routes — nothing new to set up, but that key also covers the lab's other functions; (b) a separate key that can only look at the dashboard — a little extra setup, but you can share the page with someone without giving them the lab's other access; (c) behind whatever login the engine already has, if you prefer one sign-in for everything.

What time span should the account-value-vs-SPY chart show when it first opens? (a) The whole history since the lab started — complete, but crowded and slower to draw; (b) the last 30 days — quick and readable, older detail hidden; (c) a set of buttons (1 week / 1 month / 3 months / all) so you can change it yourself — most flexible, slightly more work.

Should the page keep itself up to date? (a) Only when you reload it — simplest, never shows stale-by-surprise numbers; (b) it refreshes itself every so often while open — always current, uses a little more of the engine; (c) it updates live as things happen — most current, the most work and the most load.

How should costs be shown next to returns? (a) A single net figure — clean, but you cannot see how much costs are eating; (b) the net figure plus the gross figure and the costs subtracted, side by side — you see the drag at a glance; (c) net figure plus a small cost breakdown per period — most detail, more space used.
How much of each proposal's rationale and sources should be on the page? (a) A one-line summary per proposal — fits many proposals on screen; (b) a summary you can click to
user_feedback: Operator answers: (1) Access: the lab's existing API key, the same as its other /labs/paper routes; no new key or login. (2) Chart span: buttons for 1 week / 1 month / 3 months / all. (3) Refresh: only on reload; no auto-refresh or live updates. (4) Costs: show net return beside gross return and the costs subtracted. (5) Proposals: a one-line summary per proposal that expands on click to its full rationale and sources.
